newsitem.title: BURMA: Top Burma general issues call to crush "traitors".
newsitem.headline: Top Burma general issues call to crush "traitors".

text.p: One of Burma's military leaders blamed traitors both at home and abroad for a recent bomb blast at a fellow general's home and urged citizens to help crush this "common enemy", official media reported on Friday.

"It is evident that armed groups, expatriate groups and internal traitor groups who are supported by other countries are scheming to jeopardise national welfare," Lieutenant-General Khin Nyunt, the powerful military intelligence chief and Secretary One of the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) was quoted as saying.

Although Khin Nyung did not identify the groups, the SLORC in the past has lashed out at armed insurgency groups such as the Karen National Union and exiled groups based mainly on the Thai-Burma border for trying to destabilise the nation.
It regularly refers to the opposition National League for Democracy party led by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi as an "internal traitor group" and a "minion of neo-colonialists".
"They are acting synchronously -- with the internal minions supporting the acts of the outlawed expatriate group," Khin Nyunt said in a speech on Thursday.
"The recent bomb explosion indicated their cruel, wicked bid for assassinating leading persons of the nation."
His comments were the first direct reference by a senior SLORC official to Sunday's bombing at the house of Lieutenant-General Tin Oo, which killed Tin Oo's daughter.
The SLORC has blamed "anti-Burma" exile groups based in Japan for masterminding the bomb attack. It said the parcel bomb which killed Cho Lei Oo was sent from Japan.

The blast appeared to be the second attempt on Tin Oo's life. Tin Oo, the army chief of staff and Secretary Two of the SLORC, was the last senior official to visit a sacred Buddhist relic on Christmas Day before an explosion there.

"It is time to resolutely crush destructionists and terrorists who are marring peace and stability and hindering development of the nation by designating them as common enemy of the entire nation," Khin Nyunt said.
He also accused "neo-colonialist" radio stations of trying to cause anarchy in the country with their reports.
The government regularly attacks the Voice of America and British Broadcasting Corp, both of which broadcast Burmese- language news.

"Everybody is well aware of the neo-colonialists' radio stations broadcasting the slanderous news concocted by the subversive elements...to spread rumours to make people horrified and...to incite riot and anarchic acts...to destabilise the nation," he said.
Various SLORC leaders make speeches urging citizens to crush destructionists. Tin Oo often urges troops to "annihilate" anyone seen as trying to destabilise the nation.
